# Tagging & Environment Promotion

How releases are versioned, tagged, and promoted through the environments. This is the
day-to-day companion to the branch rules in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) (Branch Rules) and the
supervised-release flow in [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) —
this file covers **tags and promotion**, those cover **branches**.

> **DRAFT — pending governance ratification.** This documents the tag-based promotion model from
> Confluence proposal *Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)* (335216656). Four
> points **deviate from, or decide open questions in, that proposal draft** and are marked
> `⚠️ PENDING TIM` below — they are settled in-team but not yet ratified on the proposal itself.
> The squad-leads + Integration-lead review on the PR that lands this file is that ratification.
> Remove the `⚠️ PENDING TIM` callouts once signed off.

---

## Tag taxonomy

Every deployable version is an **immutable, annotated git tag**. Environments deploy a specific
tag, never "whatever's on a branch right now."

| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Cut from | Who |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | Release candidate — a stabilising snapshot, cheap to iterate | `v0.1.0-rc.2` | a commit on `release/vX.Y.Z` | **any developer** |
| `vX.Y.Z` | Final release — the exact candidate that passed every gate | `v0.1.0` | the `release/vX.Y.Z` commit merged to `main` | **tier-1-approver only** |
| `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` | Emergency fix candidate, outside the normal train | `v0.1.1-hotfix.1` | a commit on `hotfix/vX.Y.Z` | **tier-1-approver only** |

**Versioning:**
- **MAJOR** locked at `0` pre-launch (SemVer reserves `0.y.z` for initial development). `v1.0.0`
  is reserved for **go-live**; MAJOR reverts to its normal rare-breaking-change meaning after.
- **MINOR** bumps once per sprint, when a new `release/vX.Y.Z` branch is cut — sprint 1 = `v0.1.0`,
  sprint 2 = `v0.2.0`.
- **PATCH** = bug-fix-only release against an already-shipped `MAJOR.MINOR` (e.g. a hotfix after
  `v0.1.0` → `v0.1.1`).
- The `-rc.N` counter is a plain incrementing number, **not** an environment reference — the same
  `v0.1.0-rc.1` can be on Test today and SIT tomorrow. Which environment saw which candidate is
  tracked via each `deploy-*.yml`'s Actions run history, not the tag name.
- The dot in `-rc.N` matters: SemVer compares `rc.10 > rc.2` numerically only as dot-separated
  fields; `rc10`/`rc2` would sort alphabetically (wrong). This is exactly what the version-guard
  relies on.

Non-`v*` tags are a separate namespace and unaffected by any of this: `sprint/{N}/{date}` (sprint
rollover, auto-cut by `deploy-dev.yml`) and any `sit/deploy/*` refs.

---

## Cutting a tag

> ⚠️ **PENDING TIM — deviation from proposal 335216656.** The proposal prescribes `npm version`
> (which bumps `package.json` **and** creates the annotated tag in one step). We use a **tag-only
> push** instead, because `release/**` branch protection (`isAdminEnforced`, no bypass) blocks the
> `package.json`-bump *commit* that `npm version` also pushes to the branch. **Consequence:**
> `package.json`'s `version` field does **not** auto-track the release — it stays static until it is
> bumped once, deliberately, at the final-release PR. If Tim would rather keep `npm version`, the
> branch-protection model has to change (a tier-1 bypass) — see the rejected Option 2 in the rollout
> decisions.

**Release candidate (any developer):**

```bash
git checkout release/v0.1.0 && git pull
git tag -a v0.1.0-rc.0 -m "Release candidate v0.1.0-rc.0"
git push origin v0.1.0-rc.0           # tag only — NOT a branch push
gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0
```

- Always **annotated** (`-a -m`) — the tagger identity, timestamp, and message live in the tag
  object (`git show v0.1.0-rc.0`). Never lightweight.
- A tag push is not a branch push, so branch protection doesn't block it.

**Final release (tier-1-approver only):** cut `vX.Y.Z` on the release-branch commit being merged to
`main`, then promote it up UAT → Stage → Prod. Run [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)
at this point to produce the GitHub Release.

**Rollback is not a special case** — redeploy the previous known-good tag:
`gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f ref=v0.0.1`.

---

## Enforcement — what actually holds the line

> ⚠️ **Correction to proposal 335216656.** The proposal states the tag Rulesets *"genuinely
> hard-block a non-matching tag at push time"* and are *"Primary enforcement."* **That is not true on
> this org's GitHub `team` plan** — ruleset *metadata* rules (`tag_name_pattern`) are Enterprise-only
> and silently inert here (proven empirically: a malformed `v9.9-rc.0` pushed successfully while its
> deletion was blocked). Naming is enforced by the hook + workflow below, **not** the rulesets.

Three layers, in order of reliability:

1. **Pre-push hook** ([.husky/pre-push](../../.husky/pre-push) → [scripts/hooks/pre-push](../../scripts/hooks/pre-push))
   — *prevention*. Rejects a malformed `v*` tag before it leaves the developer's machine. The only
   true block on this plan. Allowed: `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`, `vX.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`. Non-`v*` tags and
   branch pushes pass through untouched.
2. **`tag-validate.yml`** ([.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml))
   — *detection*. Fails if a malformed `v*` tag lands on the remote (post-hoc alert, not a block).
3. **GitHub Rulesets** `tag-rc` (id 20487306) + `tag-release` (id 20487243) — enforce what core rules
   *can* on the `team` plan: **immutability** (`update` + `deletion` restricted) and **tier-1-only
   final tags** (`creation` restricted on `tag-release`, bypass = `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`).
   Their `tag_name_pattern` rules (`^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` and `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`)
   are **kept but inert on `team`** — they self-activate if the org ever upgrades to Enterprise.

> **Note:** GitHub ruleset objects have no free-text description field, so the "inert on team"
> caveat can't live on the ruleset itself — this section is its canonical label. The rulesets may
> optionally be *renamed* in Settings → Rules to append " — naming inert on team plan" for an
> at-a-glance signal.

---

## Environment model — two categories

| Category | Environments | How it deploys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Continuous / auto** | `dev`, `sit` | No human-picked tag. `dev` auto-deploys every `develop` merge; `sit` deploys the gate's commit via `workflow_run` off the SIT Gate on `release/**`. |
| **Tag-promoted / deliberate** | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | `workflow_dispatch` with a specific tag `ref`. Each can sit on a different tag simultaneously, decoupling their cadences. |

> ⚠️ **PENDING TIM — decides proposal Open Question 3.** The proposal's flow diagram assumed `sit`
> would become tag-triggered. **Decision: Option (b) — SIT stays branch/gate-driven** (its
> `workflow_run` trigger off the SIT Gate on `release/**` is unchanged), documented as an
> **intentional exception** to "every environment sits on a named tag." Rationale: SIT is a
> continuous auto-integration tier, same category as `dev` (which the proposal already keeps
> non-tag-based) — not a deliberate pinned-promotion tier. "Using tags" ≠ "being triggered by a tag":
> tags/Releases still exist and are visible; SIT simply auto-refreshes.

**Environment names are the real GitHub Environment names** — `dev / test / sit / uat / staging /
prod`. Tooling must key off these, not the workflow-file suffix: `deploy-stg.yml` binds
`environment: staging` (the `stg`≠`staging` mismatch already caused a bug once).

---

## Downgrade protection (version-guard)

[scripts/versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs), wired into the four tag-promoted
`deploy-*.yml` workflows:

- **`check <env> <ref>`** runs *before* the push: reads the environment's last recorded deployed tag
  and **blocks** if `ref` is semver-older (`semver.lt`). Skips non-`v*` refs, allows the first-ever
  deploy, and **fails closed** on any lookup/parse error.
- **`record <env> <ref>`** runs *after* a successful push: stamps the deployed tag as an explicit
  GitHub Deployment (the auto-created Deployment records the *trigger* ref, not the deployed tag, so
  we record it ourselves and read it back).
- **`dev` and `sit` are excluded** — they have no human-picked `ref` to compare (consistent with the
  two-category model above).
- Guard/record key off the **GitHub Environment name** (`stg`→`staging`).

---

## The Test gate

> ⚠️ **PENDING TIM — decides proposal Open Question 2.** Q1 (deploy-then-gate) **matches** the
> proposal's proposed shape. Q2 (scope) **adds bundle-size** to the proposal draft's P0-only shape:
> bundle-size is cheap, deterministic, already-wired, and mobile page-speed is a top project priority,
> so catching bloat at the earliest deployed tier is worth it.

`deploy-test.yml` runs **deploy-then-gate**: it deploys first (Test is the fast, disposable
quick-look tier), then a post-deploy gate verifies the same build. The run's overall pass/fail is the
**"safe to promote to SIT"** signal.

- **`bundle-size`** — `npm run test:max-file-size`, enforcing the `package.json` budgets
  (`main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB).
- **P0 Playwright** — attaches to the same gate once a `*.p0.spec` exists (Lead QA, gherkin-first);
  it targets the Test storefront via the `test` env's `RETAIL_APP_HOME` variable.

This intentionally differs from SIT's **gate-then-deploy** (`digital-sit.yml`), which can hang a
pre-check on a `release/**` push event that Test doesn't have.

---

## References

- Proposal: Confluence *Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)* (335216656)
- Branch rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) · supervised release: [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md)
- Implementation: [versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs) · [deploy-*.yml](../../.github/workflows/) · [tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml) · pre-push hook
- Changelog: [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)

---

_This file is Tier 1 (Governance) — changes require both squad leads and the Integration lead. It is
synced to the derived AI configs (`.cursor/rules/`, `.vscode/instructions/`,
`.github/copilot-instructions.md`) by `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs` — edit this source, then run
`npm run sync:ai-rules`._

# Tagging & Environment Promotion

day-to-day companion to the branch rules in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) (Branch Rules) and the

this file covers **tags and promotion**, those cover **branches**.

---

Every deployable version is an **immutable, annotated git tag**. Environments deploy a specific
tag, never "whatever's on a branch right now."

| `vX.Y.Z` | Final release — the exact candidate that passed every gate | `v0.1.0` | the `release/vX.Y.Z` commit merged to `main` | **tier-1-approver only** |
| `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` | Emergency fix candidate, outside the normal train | `v0.1.1-hotfix.1` | a commit on `hotfix/vX.Y.Z` | **tier-1-approver only** |

**Versioning:**
- **MAJOR** locked at `0` pre-launch (SemVer reserves `0.y.z` for initial development). `v1.0.0`
  is reserved for **go-live**; MAJOR reverts to its normal rare-breaking-change meaning after.
- **MINOR** bumps once per sprint, when a new `release/vX.Y.Z` branch is cut — sprint 1 = `v0.1.0`,
  sprint 2 = `v0.2.0`.
- **PATCH** = bug-fix-only release against an already-shipped `MAJOR.MINOR` (e.g. a hotfix after
  `v0.1.0` → `v0.1.1`).
- The `-rc.N` counter is a plain incrementing number, **not** an environment reference — the same
  `v0.1.0-rc.1` can be on Test today and SIT tomorrow. Which environment saw which candidate is
  tracked via each `deploy-*.yml`'s Actions run history, not the tag name.
- The dot in `-rc.N` matters: SemVer compares `rc.10 > rc.2` numerically only as dot-separated
  fields; `rc10`/`rc2` would sort alphabetically (wrong). This is exactly what the version-guard
  relies on.

Non-`v*` tags are a separate namespace and unaffected by any of this: `sprint/{N}/{date}` (sprint
rollover, auto-cut by `deploy-dev.yml`) and any `sit/deploy/*` refs.

---

## Cutting a tag

Tags are cut with a **tag-only push** — a raw annotated `git tag` followed by pushing the tag
alone, **not** `npm version`. `release/**` branch protection (`isAdminEnforced`, no bypass) blocks
the `package.json`-bump *commit* that `npm version` would also push to the branch, so we push the
tag by itself. **Consequence:** `package.json`'s `version` field does not auto-track each candidate

| **Continuous / auto** | `dev`, `sit` | No human-picked tag. `dev` auto-deploys every `develop` merge; `sit` deploys the gate's commit via `workflow_run` off the SIT Gate on `release/**`. |
| **Tag-promoted / deliberate** | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | `workflow_dispatch` with a specific tag `ref`. Each can sit on a different tag simultaneously, decoupling their cadences. |

**SIT stays branch/gate-driven** — its `workflow_run` trigger off the SIT Gate on `release/**` is
unchanged. This is an intentional exception to "every environment sits on a named tag": SIT is a
continuous auto-integration tier, the same category as `dev`, not a deliberate pinned-promotion
tier. Using tags is not the same as being triggered by a tag — tags and Releases still exist and are
visible; SIT simply auto-refreshes.

**Environment names are the real GitHub Environment names** — `dev / test / sit / uat / staging /
prod`. Tooling must key off these, not the workflow-file suffix: `deploy-stg.yml` binds
`environment: staging` (the `stg`≠`staging` mismatch already caused a bug once).

---

## Downgrade protection (version-guard)

[scripts/versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs), wired into the four tag-promoted
`deploy-*.yml` workflows:

- **`check <env> <ref>`** runs *before* the push: reads the environment's last recorded deployed tag
  and **blocks** if `ref` is semver-older (`semver.lt`). Skips non-`v*` refs, allows the first-ever
  deploy, and **fails closed** on any lookup/parse error.
- **`record <env> <ref>`** runs *after* a successful push: stamps the deployed tag as an explicit
  GitHub Deployment (the auto-created Deployment records the *trigger* ref, not the deployed tag, so
  we record it ourselves and read it back).
- **`dev` and `sit` are excluded** — they have no human-picked `ref` to compare (consistent with the
  two-category model above).
- Guard/record key off the **GitHub Environment name** (`stg`→`staging`).

---

## The Test gate

`deploy-test.yml` runs **deploy-then-gate**: it deploys first (Test is the fast, disposable
quick-look tier), then a post-deploy gate verifies the same build. The run's overall pass/fail is the
**"safe to promote to SIT"** signal.

- **`bundle-size`** — `npm run test:max-file-size`, enforcing the `package.json` budgets
  (`main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB). Bundle-size is cheap, deterministic, and mobile
  page-speed is a top project priority, so bloat is caught at the earliest deployed tier.
- **P0 Playwright** — attaches to the same gate once a `*.p0.spec` exists (Lead QA, gherkin-first);
  it targets the Test storefront via the `test` env's `RETAIL_APP_HOME` variable.

This intentionally differs from SIT's **gate-then-deploy** (`digital-sit.yml`), which can hang a
pre-check on a `release/**` push event that Test doesn't have.

228	/**
229	 * Strip existing frontmatter (content between the first pair of --- lines) from a markdown string.
230	 * Returns the body content without frontmatter.
231	 */
232	function stripFrontmatter(content) {
233	    const lines = content.split('\n')
234	    if (lines[0].trim() !== '---') {
235	        return content
236	    }
237	    const closingIndex = lines.findIndex((line, i) => i > 0 && line.trim() === '---')
238	    if (closingIndex === -1) {
239	        return content
240	    }
241	    return lines.slice(closingIndex + 1).join('\n').trimStart()

245	 * Extract a single field value from a markdown file's YAML frontmatter.
246	 * Returns null if no frontmatter exists or the field is not present.
247	 */
248	function extractFrontmatterField(content, field) {
249	    const lines = content.split('\n')
250	    if (lines[0].trim() !== '---') return null
251	    const closingIndex = lines.findIndex((line, i) => i > 0 && line.trim() === '---')
252	    if (closingIndex === -1) return null
253	    const fmLines = lines.slice(1, closingIndex)
254	    const match = fmLines
255	        .map((line) => line.match(new RegExp(`^${field}:\\s*(.*)$`)))
256	        .find((m) => m !== null)
257	    return match ? match[1].trim() : null
258	}

262	 * Returns 0 if the file does not exist.

267	    } catch {

270	}

274	 */
275	function formatTimeDiff(ms) {
276	    const seconds = Math.round(ms / 1000)
277	    const minutes = Math.round(seconds / 60)
278	    const hours = Math.round(minutes / 60)
279	    const days = Math.round(hours / 24)
280	    if (days > 0) return `${days} day${days === 1 ? '' : 's'} newer`
281	    if (hours > 0) return `${hours} hour${hours === 1 ? '' : 's'} newer`
282	    if (minutes > 0) return `${minutes} minute${minutes === 1 ? '' : 's'} newer`
283	    return `${seconds} second${seconds === 1 ? '' : 's'} newer`
284	}

294	        targetMissing: [],

296	    }

299	        const sources = Array.isArray(entry.source) ? entry.source : [entry.source]
300	        const targetPath = path.join(ROOT, entry.target)
301	
302	        // Check all sources exist
303	        const missingSources = sources.filter((s) => !fs.existsSync(path.join(ROOT, s)))
304	        if (missingSources.length > 0) {
305	            results.sourceMissing.push({entry, reason: `source file(s) not found: ${missingSources.join(', ')}`})
306	            continue
307	        }
308	
309	        // Check target exists
310	        if (!fs.existsSync(targetPath)) {
311	            results.targetMissing.push({entry, reason: 'target file does not exist yet'})
312	            if (isFix) {
313	                regenerateTarget(entry)
314	                console.log(`  Created: ${entry.target}`)
315	            }
316	            continue
317	        }
318	
319	        // For array sources: use the mtime of the newest source file as the comparison point
320	        const sourceMtime = Math.max(...sources.map((s) => getMtime(path.join(ROOT, s))))
321	        const targetMtime = getMtime(targetPath)
322	
323	        if (sourceMtime > targetMtime) {
324	            const diff = sourceMtime - targetMtime
325	            results.driftDetected.push({entry, diff})
326	            if (isFix) {
327	                regenerateTarget(entry)
328	                console.log(`  Regenerated: ${entry.target}`)
329	            }
330	        } else {
331	            results.upToDate.push(entry)
332	        }
333	    }
334	
335	    // Classify entries by mode for grouped reporting
336	    const ruleEntries = MANIFEST.filter((e) => e.mode === 'rule')
337	    const skillEntries = MANIFEST.filter((e) => e.mode === 'skill')
338	    const compileEntries = MANIFEST.filter((e) => e.mode === 'compile')
339	
340	    const statusIcon = (entry) => {
341	        const inDrift = results.driftDetected.some((r) => r.entry.target === entry.target)
342	        const inMissing = results.targetMissing.some((r) => r.entry.target === entry.target)
343	        const inSourceMissing = results.sourceMissing.some((r) => r.entry.target === entry.target)
344	        if (inSourceMissing) return '❓'
345	        if (inMissing) return '❗'
346	        if (inDrift) return '⚠️ '
347	        return '✅'
348	    }
349	
350	    const printSection = (label, entries) => {
351	        console.log(`\n${label} (${entries.length}):`)
352	        for (const entry of entries) {
353	            const driftEntry = results.driftDetected.find((r) => r.entry.target === entry.target)
354	            const suffix = driftEntry ? ` (source is ${formatTimeDiff(driftEntry.diff)})` : ''
355	            console.log(`  ${statusIcon(entry)} ${entry.target}${suffix}`)
356	        }
357	    }

362	    printSection('Skills (.cursor/rules/skills/*.mdc)', skillEntries)
363	    printSection('Copilot / VS Code (compiled)', compileEntries)
364	
365	    const totalDrift = results.driftDetected.length
366	    const totalMissing = results.targetMissing.length
367	    const totalSourceMissing = results.sourceMissing.length
368	
369	    console.log('')
370	    if (totalDrift === 0 && totalMissing === 0 && totalSourceMissing === 0) {
371	        console.log('All targets are in sync with their .claude/ sources.')
372	    } else {
373	        if (totalMissing > 0) {
374	            console.log(`❗ Target missing: ${totalMissing} file(s)`)
375	            for (const {entry} of results.targetMissing) {
376	                console.log(`  - ${entry.target}`)
377	            }
378	        }
379	        if (totalSourceMissing > 0) {
380	            console.log(`❓ Source missing: ${totalSourceMissing} file(s)`)
381	            for (const {entry, reason} of results.sourceMissing) {
382	                console.log(`  - ${entry.target}: ${reason} (check MANIFEST)`)
383	            }
384	        }
385	        if (!isFix && (totalDrift > 0 || totalMissing > 0)) {
386	            console.log('\nRun with --fix to regenerate.')
387	        }
388	    }
389	
390	    // Exit with code 1 in --check mode if any drift or missing targets
391	    if (isCheck) {
392	        const hasDrift =
393	            results.driftDetected.length > 0 ||
394	            results.targetMissing.length > 0 ||
395	            results.sourceMissing.length > 0
396	        if (hasDrift) {
397	            process.exit(1)
398	        }
399	    }
400	}

402	/**
403	 * Regenerate a target file from its source(s). Dispatches on entry.mode:
404	 *   - 'rule':    single source, full Cursor frontmatter from manifest
405	 *   - 'skill':   single source, description extracted from source frontmatter
406	 *   - 'compile': multi-source concatenation, plain markdown (no Cursor frontmatter)
407	 */
408	function regenerateTarget(entry) {
409	    const sources = Array.isArray(entry.source) ? entry.source : [entry.source]
410	    const targetPath = path.join(ROOT, entry.target)
411	    const syncList = sources.join(', ')
412	    const syncedFromComment = `<!-- synced-from: ${syncList} — edit the source(s), not this file, then run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix -->`
413	
414	    let output
415	
416	    if (entry.mode === 'rule') {
417	        const body = stripFrontmatter(fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, sources[0]), 'utf8'))
418	        const frontmatter = buildFrontmatter(entry.frontmatter)
419	        output = `${frontmatter}\n${syncedFromComment}\n\n${body}`
420	    } else if (entry.mode === 'skill') {
421	        const sourceContent = fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, sources[0]), 'utf8')
422	        const description = extractFrontmatterField(sourceContent, 'description')
423	        if (!description) {
424	            throw new Error(`Skill source ${sources[0]} is missing a 'description' field in its frontmatter`)
425	        }
426	        const body = stripFrontmatter(sourceContent)
427	        const frontmatter = buildFrontmatter({
428	            description,
429	            globs: entry.frontmatter?.globs ?? '',
430	            alwaysApply: entry.frontmatter?.alwaysApply ?? false
431	        })
432	        output = `${frontmatter}\n${syncedFromComment}\n\n${body}`
433	    } else if (entry.mode === 'compile') {
434	        const parts = sources.map((s) => {
435	            const body = stripFrontmatter(fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, s), 'utf8')).trim()
436	            return `<!-- from: ${s} -->\n\n${body}`
437	        })
438	        const title = entry.title ? `# ${entry.title}\n\n` : ''
439	        output = `${syncedFromComment}\n\n${title}${parts.join('\n\n---\n\n')}\n`
440	    } else {
441	        throw new Error(`Unknown mode '${entry.mode}' for target ${entry.target}`)
442	    }
443	
444	    const targetDir = path.dirname(targetPath)
445	    if (!fs.existsSync(targetDir)) {
446	        fs.mkdirSync(targetDir, {recursive: true})
447	    }
448	    fs.writeFileSync(targetPath, output, 'utf8')
449	}
450	
451	main()

# Tagging & Environment Promotion

How releases are versioned, tagged, and promoted through the environments. This is the
day-to-day companion to the branch rules in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) (Branch Rules) and the
supervised-release flow in [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) —
this file covers **tags and promotion**, those cover **branches**.

---

## Tag taxonomy

Every deployable version is an **immutable, annotated git tag**. Environments deploy a specific
tag, never "whatever's on a branch right now."

| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Cut from | Who |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | Release candidate — a stabilising snapshot, cheap to iterate | `v0.1.0-rc.2` | a commit on `release/vX.Y.Z` | **any developer** |
| `vX.Y.Z` | Final release — the exact candidate that passed every gate | `v0.1.0` | the `release/vX.Y.Z` commit merged to `main` | **tier-1-approver only** |
| `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` | Emergency fix candidate, outside the normal train | `v0.1.1-hotfix.1` | a commit on `hotfix/vX.Y.Z` | **tier-1-approver only** |

**Versioning:**
- **MAJOR** locked at `0` pre-launch (SemVer reserves `0.y.z` for initial development). `v1.0.0`
  is reserved for **go-live**; MAJOR reverts to its normal rare-breaking-change meaning after.
- **MINOR** bumps once per sprint, when a new `release/vX.Y.Z` branch is cut — sprint 1 = `v0.1.0`,
  sprint 2 = `v0.2.0`.
- **PATCH** = bug-fix-only release against an already-shipped `MAJOR.MINOR` (e.g. a hotfix after
  `v0.1.0` → `v0.1.1`).
- The `-rc.N` counter is a plain incrementing number, **not** an environment reference — the same
  `v0.1.0-rc.1` can be on Test today and SIT tomorrow. Which environment saw which candidate is
  tracked via each `deploy-*.yml`'s Actions run history, not the tag name.
- The dot in `-rc.N` matters: SemVer compares `rc.10 > rc.2` numerically only as dot-separated
  fields; `rc10`/`rc2` would sort alphabetically (wrong). This is exactly what the version-guard
  relies on.

Non-`v*` tags are a separate namespace and unaffected by any of this: `sprint/{N}/{date}` (sprint
rollover, auto-cut by `deploy-dev.yml`) and any `sit/deploy/*` refs.

---

## Cutting a tag

Tags are cut with a **tag-only push** — a raw annotated `git tag` followed by pushing the tag
alone, **not** `npm version`. `release/**` branch protection (`isAdminEnforced`, no bypass) blocks
the `package.json`-bump *commit* that `npm version` would also push to the branch, so we push the
tag by itself. **Consequence:** `package.json`'s `version` field does not auto-track each candidate
— it is bumped once, deliberately, at the final-release PR.

**Release candidate (any developer):**

```bash
git checkout release/v0.1.0 && git pull
git tag -a v0.1.0-rc.0 -m "Release candidate v0.1.0-rc.0"
git push origin v0.1.0-rc.0           # tag only — NOT a branch push
gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0
```

- Always **annotated** (`-a -m`) — the tagger identity, timestamp, and message live in the tag
  object (`git show v0.1.0-rc.0`). Never lightweight.
- A tag push is not a branch push, so branch protection doesn't block it.

**Final release (tier-1-approver only):** cut `vX.Y.Z` on the release-branch commit being merged to
`main`, then promote it up UAT → Stage → Prod. Run [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)
at this point to produce the GitHub Release.

**Rollback is not a special case** — redeploy the previous known-good tag:
`gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f ref=v0.0.1`.

---

## Enforcement — what actually holds the line

On this org's GitHub **`team`** plan, ruleset *metadata* rules (`tag_name_pattern`) are
Enterprise-only and silently **inert** — a malformed `v*` tag is not blocked at push time by a
ruleset. Naming is enforced by the hook and workflow below, not the rulesets. Three layers, in
order of reliability:

1. **Pre-push hook** ([.husky/pre-push](../../.husky/pre-push) → [scripts/hooks/pre-push](../../scripts/hooks/pre-push))
   — *prevention*. Rejects a malformed `v*` tag before it leaves the developer's machine. The only
   true block on this plan. Allowed: `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`, `vX.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`. Non-`v*` tags and
   branch pushes pass through untouched.
2. **`tag-validate.yml`** ([.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml))
   — *detection*. Fails if a malformed `v*` tag lands on the remote (post-hoc alert, not a block).
3. **GitHub Rulesets** `tag-rc` (id 20487306) + `tag-release` (id 20487243) — enforce what core rules
   *can* on the `team` plan: **immutability** (`update` + `deletion` restricted) and **tier-1-only
   final tags** (`creation` restricted on `tag-release`, bypass = `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`).
   Their `tag_name_pattern` rules (`^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` and `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`)
   are **kept but inert on `team`** — they self-activate if the org ever upgrades to Enterprise.

GitHub ruleset objects have no free-text description field, so the "inert on team" caveat can't
live on the ruleset itself — this section is its canonical record. The rulesets may optionally be
renamed in Settings → Rules to append " — naming inert on team plan" for an at-a-glance signal.

---

## Environment model — two categories

| Category | Environments | How it deploys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Continuous / auto** | `dev`, `sit` | No human-picked tag. `dev` auto-deploys every `develop` merge; `sit` deploys the gate's commit via `workflow_run` off the SIT Gate on `release/**`. |
| **Tag-promoted / deliberate** | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | `workflow_dispatch` with a specific tag `ref`. Each can sit on a different tag simultaneously, decoupling their cadences. |

**SIT stays branch/gate-driven** — its `workflow_run` trigger off the SIT Gate on `release/**` is
unchanged. This is an intentional exception to "every environment sits on a named tag": SIT is a
continuous auto-integration tier, the same category as `dev`, not a deliberate pinned-promotion
tier. Using tags is not the same as being triggered by a tag — tags and Releases still exist and are
visible; SIT simply auto-refreshes.

**Environment names are the real GitHub Environment names** — `dev / test / sit / uat / staging /
prod`. Tooling must key off these, not the workflow-file suffix: `deploy-stg.yml` binds
`environment: staging` (the `stg`≠`staging` mismatch already caused a bug once).

---

## Downgrade protection (version-guard)

[scripts/versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs), wired into the four tag-promoted
`deploy-*.yml` workflows:

- **`check <env> <ref>`** runs *before* the push: reads the environment's last recorded deployed tag
  and **blocks** if `ref` is semver-older (`semver.lt`). Skips non-`v*` refs, allows the first-ever
  deploy, and **fails closed** on any lookup/parse error.
- **`record <env> <ref>`** runs *after* a successful push: stamps the deployed tag as an explicit
  GitHub Deployment (the auto-created Deployment records the *trigger* ref, not the deployed tag, so
  we record it ourselves and read it back).
- **`dev` and `sit` are excluded** — they have no human-picked `ref` to compare (consistent with the
  two-category model above).
- Guard/record key off the **GitHub Environment name** (`stg`→`staging`).

---

## The Test gate

`deploy-test.yml` runs **deploy-then-gate**: it deploys first (Test is the fast, disposable
quick-look tier), then a post-deploy gate verifies the same build. The run's overall pass/fail is the
**"safe to promote to SIT"** signal.

- **`bundle-size`** — `npm run test:max-file-size`, enforcing the `package.json` budgets
  (`main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB). Bundle-size is cheap, deterministic, and mobile
  page-speed is a top project priority, so bloat is caught at the earliest deployed tier.
- **P0 Playwright** — attaches to the same gate once a `*.p0.spec` exists (Lead QA, gherkin-first);
  it targets the Test storefront via the `test` env's `RETAIL_APP_HOME` variable.

This intentionally differs from SIT's **gate-then-deploy** (`digital-sit.yml`), which can hang a
pre-check on a `release/**` push event that Test doesn't have.

---

## References

- Design: Confluence *Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)* (335216656)
- Branch rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) · supervised release: [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md)
- Implementation: [versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs) · [deploy-*.yml](../../.github/workflows/) · [tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml) · pre-push hook
- Changelog: [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)

# Tagging & Environment Promotion

How releases are versioned, tagged, and promoted through the environments. This is the
day-to-day companion to the branch rules in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) (Branch Rules) and the
supervised-release flow in [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) —
this file covers **tags and promotion**, those cover **branches**.

---

## Tag taxonomy

Every deployable version is an **immutable, annotated git tag**. Environments deploy a specific
tag, never "whatever's on a branch right now."

| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Cut from | Who |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | Release candidate — a stabilising snapshot, cheap to iterate | `v0.1.0-rc.2` | a commit on `release/vX.Y.Z` | **any developer** |
| `vX.Y.Z` | Final release — the exact candidate that passed every gate | `v0.1.0` | the `release/vX.Y.Z` commit merged to `main` | **tier-1-approver only** |
| `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` | Emergency fix candidate, outside the normal train | `v0.1.1-hotfix.1` | a commit on `hotfix/vX.Y.Z` | **tier-1-approver only** |

**Versioning:**
- **MAJOR** locked at `0` pre-launch (SemVer reserves `0.y.z` for initial development). `v1.0.0`
  is reserved for **go-live**; MAJOR reverts to its normal rare-breaking-change meaning after.
- **MINOR** bumps once per sprint, when a new `release/vX.Y.Z` branch is cut — sprint 1 = `v0.1.0`,
  sprint 2 = `v0.2.0`.
- **PATCH** = bug-fix-only release against an already-shipped `MAJOR.MINOR` (e.g. a hotfix after
  `v0.1.0` → `v0.1.1`).
- The `-rc.N` counter is a plain incrementing number, **not** an environment reference — the same
  `v0.1.0-rc.1` can be on Test today and SIT tomorrow. Which environment saw which candidate is
  tracked via each `deploy-*.yml`'s Actions run history, not the tag name.
- The dot in `-rc.N` matters: SemVer compares `rc.10 > rc.2` numerically only as dot-separated
  fields; `rc10`/`rc2` would sort alphabetically (wrong). This is exactly what the version-guard
  relies on.

Non-`v*` tags are a separate namespace and unaffected by any of this: `sprint/{N}/{date}` (sprint
rollover, auto-cut by `deploy-dev.yml`) and any `sit/deploy/*` refs.

---

## Cutting a tag

Tags are cut with a **tag-only push** — a raw annotated `git tag`, then pushing the tag alone. We
deliberately avoid `npm version`: it creates a local `package.json`-bump *commit* alongside the tag,
and pushing that commit to the release branch is blocked by `release/**` branch protection
(`isAdminEnforced`, no bypass). Pushing only the tag sidesteps this — a tag push is not a branch
push. **Consequence:** `package.json`'s `version` field does not auto-track each candidate — it is
bumped once, deliberately, at the final-release PR.

**Release candidate (any developer):**

```bash
git checkout release/v0.1.0 && git pull
git tag -a v0.1.0-rc.0 -m "Release candidate v0.1.0-rc.0"
git push origin v0.1.0-rc.0           # tag only — NOT a branch push
gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0
```

- Always **annotated** (`-a -m`) — the tagger identity, timestamp, and message live in the tag
  object (`git show v0.1.0-rc.0`). Never lightweight.
- A tag push is not a branch push, so branch protection doesn't block it.

**Final release (tier-1-approver only):** cut `vX.Y.Z` on the release-branch commit being merged to
`main`, then promote it up UAT → Stage → Prod. Run [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)
at this point to produce the GitHub Release.

**Rollback is not a special case** — redeploy the previous known-good tag:
`gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f ref=v0.0.1`.

---

## Enforcement — what actually holds the line

On this org's GitHub **`team`** plan, ruleset *metadata* rules (`tag_name_pattern`) are
Enterprise-only and silently **inert** — a malformed `v*` tag is not blocked at push time by a
ruleset. Naming is enforced by the hook and workflow below, not the rulesets. Three layers, in
order of reliability:

1. **Pre-push hook** ([.husky/pre-push](../../.husky/pre-push) → [scripts/hooks/pre-push](../../scripts/hooks/pre-push))
   — *best-effort prevention*. Rejects a malformed `v*` tag before it leaves the developer's machine
   — the earliest catch, but bypassable (`git push --no-verify`, or a checkout without the hook
   installed), so not a hard guarantee. Allowed: `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`, `vX.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`.
   Non-`v*` tags and branch pushes pass through untouched.
2. **`tag-validate.yml`** ([.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml))
   — *detection*. Fails if a malformed `v*` tag lands on the remote (post-hoc alert, not a block).
3. **GitHub Rulesets** `tag-rc` (id 20487306) + `tag-release` (id 20487243) — enforce what core rules
   *can* on the `team` plan: **immutability** (`update` + `deletion` restricted) and **tier-1-only
   final tags** (`creation` restricted on `tag-release`, bypass = `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`).
   Their `tag_name_pattern` rules (`^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` and `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`)
   are **kept but inert on `team`** — they self-activate if the org ever upgrades to Enterprise.

GitHub ruleset objects have no free-text description field, so the "inert on team" caveat can't
live on the ruleset itself — this section is its canonical record. The rulesets may optionally be
renamed in Settings → Rules to append " — naming inert on team plan" for an at-a-glance signal.

---

## Environment model — two categories

| Category | Environments | How it deploys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Continuous / auto** | `dev`, `sit` | No human-picked tag. `dev` auto-deploys every `develop` merge; `sit` deploys the gate's commit via `workflow_run` off the SIT Gate on `release/**`. |
| **Tag-promoted / deliberate** | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | `workflow_dispatch` with a specific tag `ref`. Each can sit on a different tag simultaneously, decoupling their cadences. |

**SIT stays branch/gate-driven** — its `workflow_run` trigger off the SIT Gate on `release/**` is
unchanged. This is an intentional exception to "every environment sits on a named tag": SIT is a
continuous auto-integration tier, the same category as `dev`, not a deliberate pinned-promotion
tier. Using tags is not the same as being triggered by a tag — tags and Releases still exist and are
visible; SIT simply auto-refreshes.

**Environment names are the real GitHub Environment names** — `dev / test / sit / uat / staging /
prod`. Tooling must key off these, not the workflow-file suffix: `deploy-stg.yml` binds
`environment: staging` (the `stg`≠`staging` mismatch already caused a bug once).

---

## Downgrade protection (version-guard)

[scripts/versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs), wired into the four tag-promoted
`deploy-*.yml` workflows:

- **`check <env> <ref>`** runs *before* the push: reads the environment's last recorded deployed tag
  and **blocks** if `ref` is semver-older (`semver.lt`). Skips non-`v*` refs, allows the first-ever
  deploy, and **fails closed** on any lookup/parse error.
- **`record <env> <ref>`** runs *after* a successful push: stamps the deployed tag as an explicit
  GitHub Deployment (the auto-created Deployment records the *trigger* ref, not the deployed tag, so
  we record it ourselves and read it back).
- **`dev` and `sit` are excluded** — they have no human-picked `ref` to compare (consistent with the
  two-category model above).
- Guard/record key off the **GitHub Environment name** (`stg`→`staging`).

---

## The Test gate

`deploy-test.yml` runs **deploy-then-gate**: it deploys first (Test is the fast, disposable
quick-look tier), then a post-deploy gate verifies the same build. The run's overall pass/fail is the
**"safe to promote to SIT"** signal.

- **`bundle-size`** — `npm run test:max-file-size`, enforcing the `package.json` budgets
  (`main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB). Bundle-size is cheap, deterministic, and mobile
  page-speed is a top project priority, so bloat is caught at the earliest deployed tier.
- **P0 Playwright** — attaches to the same gate once a `*.p0.spec` exists (Lead QA, gherkin-first);
  it targets the Test storefront via the `test` env's `RETAIL_APP_HOME` variable.

This intentionally differs from SIT's **gate-then-deploy** (`digital-sit.yml`), which can hang a
pre-check on a `release/**` push event that Test doesn't have.

---

## References

- Design: Confluence *Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)* (335216656)
- Branch rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) · supervised release: [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md)
- Implementation: [versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs) · [deploy-*.yml](../../.github/workflows/) · [tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml) · pre-push hook
- Changelog: [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# pre-push — reject malformed version tags (v*) before they leave this machine.
3	#
4	# Why this exists: on the GitHub Team plan, repository-ruleset `tag_name_pattern`
5	# rules are NOT enforced (they are an Enterprise-only feature), so this client-side
6	# hook is the primary *prevention* for tag naming. The `tag-validate.yml` workflow is
7	# the post-push safety net (it can only flag, not block, since it runs after the push).
8	#
9	# Allowed:   vX.Y.Z-rc.N      (release candidate)
10	#            vX.Y.Z           (final)
11	#            vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N  (hotfix)
12	# Untouched: any non-v* tag (e.g. sprint/*, sit/deploy/*) and all branch pushes.
13	#
14	# git passes the refs being pushed on stdin as:
15	#   <local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>
16	# Key on the REMOTE ref — that's the ref being created on the remote, so it also
17	# catches `git push origin <branch>:refs/tags/vX` where the local ref isn't a tag.
18	# A deletion has local_ref == "(delete)"; skip those (tag deletion is governed by
19	# the ruleset and must not be blocked here).
20	rc_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-rc\.[0-9]+$'
21	final_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-hotfix\.[0-9]+)?$'
22	status=0
23	
24	while read -r local_ref _lsha remote_ref _rsha; do

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pre-push — reject malformed version tags (v*) before they leave this machine.
#
# Why this exists: on the GitHub Team plan, repository-ruleset `tag_name_pattern`
# rules are NOT enforced (they are an Enterprise-only feature), so this client-side
# hook is the primary *prevention* for tag naming. The `tag-validate.yml` workflow is
# the post-push safety net (it can only flag, not block, since it runs after the push).
#
# Allowed:   vX.Y.Z-rc.N      (release candidate)
#            vX.Y.Z           (final)
#            vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N  (hotfix)
# Untouched: any non-v* tag (e.g. sprint/*, sit/deploy/*) and all branch pushes.
#
# git passes the refs being pushed on stdin as:
#   <local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>
# Key on the REMOTE ref — that's the ref being created on the remote, so it also
# catches `git push origin <branch>:refs/tags/vX` where the local ref isn't a tag.
# A deletion has local_ref == "(delete)"; skip those (tag deletion is governed by
# the ruleset and must not be blocked here).
rc_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-rc\.[0-9]+$'
final_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-hotfix\.[0-9]+)?$'
status=0

while read -r local_ref _lsha remote_ref _rsha; do
  case "$remote_ref" in
    refs/tags/v*)
      tag=${remote_ref#refs/tags/}
      if [[ "$local_ref" != "(delete)" ]] && [[ ! $tag =~ $rc_re && ! $tag =~ $final_re ]]; then
        echo "✗ pre-push: refusing malformed version tag '$tag'" >&2
        echo "  allowed: vX.Y.Z-rc.N | vX.Y.Z | vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N" >&2
        status=1
      fi
      ;;
  esac
done

exit $status

1	# Tagging & Environment Promotion
2	
3	How releases are versioned, tagged, and promoted through the environments. This is the
4	day-to-day companion to the branch rules in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) (Branch Rules) and the
5	supervised-release flow in [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) —
6	this file covers **tags and promotion**, those cover **branches**.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Tag taxonomy
11	
12	Every deployable version is an **immutable, annotated git tag**. Environments deploy a specific
13	tag, never "whatever's on a branch right now."
14	
15	| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Cut from | Who |
16	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
17	| `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | Release candidate — a stabilising snapshot, cheap to iterate | `v0.1.0-rc.2` | a commit on `release/vX.Y.Z` | **any developer** |
18	| `vX.Y.Z` | Final release — the exact candidate that passed every gate | `v0.1.0` | the `release/vX.Y.Z` commit merged to `main` | **tier-1-approver only** |
19	| `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` | Emergency fix candidate, outside the normal train | `v0.1.1-hotfix.1` | a commit on `hotfix/vX.Y.Z` | **tier-1-approver only** |
20	
21	**Versioning:**
22	- **MAJOR** locked at `0` pre-launch (SemVer reserves `0.y.z` for initial development). `v1.0.0`
23	  is reserved for **go-live**; MAJOR reverts to its normal rare-breaking-change meaning after.
24	- **MINOR** bumps once per sprint, when a new `release/vX.Y.Z` branch is cut — sprint 1 = `v0.1.0`,
25	  sprint 2 = `v0.2.0`.
26	- **PATCH** = bug-fix-only release against an already-shipped `MAJOR.MINOR` (e.g. a hotfix after
27	  `v0.1.0` → `v0.1.1`).
28	- The `-rc.N` counter is a plain incrementing number, **not** an environment reference — the same
29	  `v0.1.0-rc.1` can be on Test today and SIT tomorrow. Which environment saw which candidate is
30	  tracked via each `deploy-*.yml`'s Actions run history, not the tag name.
31	- The dot in `-rc.N` matters: SemVer compares `rc.10 > rc.2` numerically only as dot-separated
32	  fields; `rc10`/`rc2` would sort alphabetically (wrong). This is exactly what the version-guard
33	  relies on.
34	
35	Non-`v*` tags are a separate namespace and unaffected by any of this: `sprint/{N}/{date}` (sprint
36	rollover, auto-cut by `deploy-dev.yml`) and any `sit/deploy/*` refs.
37	
38	---
39	
40	## Cutting a tag
41	
42	Tags are cut with a **tag-only push** — a raw annotated `git tag`, then pushing the tag alone. We
43	deliberately avoid `npm version`: it creates a local `package.json`-bump *commit* alongside the tag,
44	and pushing that commit to the release branch is blocked by `release/**` branch protection
45	(`isAdminEnforced`, no bypass). Pushing only the tag sidesteps this — a tag push is not a branch
46	push. **Consequence:** `package.json`'s `version` field does not auto-track each candidate — it is
47	bumped once, deliberately, at the final-release PR.
48	
49	**Release candidate (any developer):**
50	
51	```bash
52	git checkout release/v0.1.0 && git pull
53	git tag -a v0.1.0-rc.0 -m "Release candidate v0.1.0-rc.0"
54	git push origin v0.1.0-rc.0           # tag only — NOT a branch push
55	gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0
56	```
57	
58	- Always **annotated** (`-a -m`) — the tagger identity, timestamp, and message live in the tag
59	  object (`git show v0.1.0-rc.0`). Never lightweight.
60	- A tag push is not a branch push, so branch protection doesn't block it.
61	
62	**Final release (tier-1-approver only):** cut `vX.Y.Z` on the release-branch commit being merged to
63	`main`, then promote it up UAT → Stage → Prod. Run [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)
64	at this point to produce the GitHub Release.
65	
66	**Rollback is not a special case** — redeploy the previous known-good tag:
67	`gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f ref=v0.0.1`.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Enforcement — what actually holds the line
72	
73	On this org's GitHub **`team`** plan, ruleset *metadata* rules (`tag_name_pattern`) are
74	Enterprise-only and silently **inert** — a malformed `v*` tag is not blocked at push time by a
75	ruleset. Naming is enforced by the hook and workflow below, not the rulesets. Three layers, in
76	order of reliability:
77	
78	1. **Pre-push hook** ([.husky/pre-push](../../.husky/pre-push) → [scripts/hooks/pre-push](../../scripts/hooks/pre-push))
79	   — *best-effort prevention*. Rejects a malformed `v*` tag before it leaves the developer's machine
80	   — the earliest catch, but bypassable (`git push --no-verify`, or a checkout without the hook
81	   installed), so not a hard guarantee. Allowed: `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`, `vX.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`.
82	   Non-`v*` tags and branch pushes pass through untouched.
83	2. **`tag-validate.yml`** ([.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml))
84	   — *detection*. Fails if a malformed `v*` tag lands on the remote (post-hoc alert, not a block).
85	3. **GitHub Rulesets** `tag-rc` (id 20487306) + `tag-release` (id 20487243) — enforce what core rules
86	   *can* on the `team` plan: **immutability** (`update` + `deletion` restricted) and **tier-1-only
87	   final tags** (`creation` restricted on `tag-release`, bypass = `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`).
88	   Their `tag_name_pattern` rules (`^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` and `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`)
89	   are **kept but inert on `team`** — they self-activate if the org ever upgrades to Enterprise.
90	
91	GitHub ruleset objects have no free-text description field, so the "inert on team" caveat can't
92	live on the ruleset itself — this section is its canonical record. The rulesets may optionally be
93	renamed in Settings → Rules to append " — naming inert on team plan" for an at-a-glance signal.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## Environment model — two categories
98	
99	| Category | Environments | How it deploys |
100	| --- | --- | --- |
101	| **Continuous / auto** | `dev`, `sit` | No human-picked tag. `dev` auto-deploys every `develop` merge; `sit` deploys the gate's commit via `workflow_run` off the SIT Gate on `release/**`. |
102	| **Tag-promoted / deliberate** | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | `workflow_dispatch` with a specific tag `ref`. Each can sit on a different tag simultaneously, decoupling their cadences. |
103	
104	**SIT stays branch/gate-driven** — its `workflow_run` trigger off the SIT Gate on `release/**` is
105	unchanged. This is an intentional exception to "every environment sits on a named tag": SIT is a
106	continuous auto-integration tier, the same category as `dev`, not a deliberate pinned-promotion
107	tier. Using tags is not the same as being triggered by a tag — tags and Releases still exist and are
108	visible; SIT simply auto-refreshes.
109	
110	**Environment names are the real GitHub Environment names** — `dev / test / sit / uat / staging /
111	prod`. Tooling must key off these, not the workflow-file suffix: `deploy-stg.yml` binds
112	`environment: staging` (the `stg`≠`staging` mismatch already caused a bug once).
113	
114	---
115	
116	## Downgrade protection (version-guard)
117	
118	[scripts/versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs), wired into the four tag-promoted
119	`deploy-*.yml` workflows:
120	
121	- **`check <env> <ref>`** runs *before* the push: reads the environment's last recorded deployed tag
122	  and **blocks** if `ref` is semver-older (`semver.lt`). Skips non-`v*` refs, allows the first-ever
123	  deploy, and **fails closed** on any lookup/parse error.
124	- **`record <env> <ref>`** runs *after* a successful push: stamps the deployed tag as an explicit
125	  GitHub Deployment (the auto-created Deployment records the *trigger* ref, not the deployed tag, so
126	  we record it ourselves and read it back).
127	- **`dev` and `sit` are excluded** — they have no human-picked `ref` to compare (consistent with the
128	  two-category model above).
129	- Guard/record key off the **GitHub Environment name** (`stg`→`staging`).
130	
131	---
132	
133	## The Test gate
134	
135	`deploy-test.yml` runs **deploy-then-gate**: it deploys first (Test is the fast, disposable
136	quick-look tier), then a post-deploy gate verifies the same build. The run's overall pass/fail is the

29	  `v0.1.0-rc.1` can be on Test today and SIT tomorrow. Which environment saw which candidate is
30	  tracked via each `deploy-*.yml`'s Actions run history, not the tag name.
31	- The dot in `-rc.N` matters: SemVer compares `rc.10 > rc.2` numerically only as dot-separated
32	  fields; `rc10`/`rc2` would sort alphabetically (wrong). This is exactly what the version-guard
33	  relies on.
34	
35	Non-`v*` tags are a separate namespace and unaffected by any of this: `sprint/{N}/{date}` (sprint
36	rollover, auto-cut by `deploy-dev.yml`) and any `sit/deploy/*` refs.
37	
38	---
39	
40	## Cutting a tag
41	
42	Tags are cut with a **tag-only push** — a raw annotated `git tag`, then pushing the tag alone. We
43	deliberately avoid `npm version`: it creates a local `package.json`-bump *commit* alongside the tag,
44	and pushing that commit to the release branch is blocked by `release/**` branch protection
45	(`isAdminEnforced`, no bypass). Pushing only the tag sidesteps this — a tag push is not a branch
46	push. **Consequence:** `package.json`'s `version` field does not auto-track each candidate — it is
47	bumped once, deliberately, at the final-release PR.
48	
49	**Release candidate (any developer):**
50	
51	```bash
52	git checkout release/v0.1.0 && git pull
53	git tag -a v0.1.0-rc.0 -m "Release candidate v0.1.0-rc.0"
54	git push origin v0.1.0-rc.0           # tag only — NOT a branch push
55	gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0
56	```
57	
58	- Always **annotated** (`-a -m`) — the tagger identity, timestamp, and message live in the tag
59	  object (`git show v0.1.0-rc.0`). Never lightweight.
60	- A tag push is not a branch push, so branch protection doesn't block it.
61	
62	**Final release (tier-1-approver only):** cut `vX.Y.Z` on the release-branch commit being merged to
63	`main`, then promote it up UAT → Stage → Prod. Run [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)
64	at this point to produce the GitHub Release.
65	
66	**Rollback is not a special case** — redeploy the previous known-good tag:
67	`gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f ref=v0.0.1`.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Enforcement — what actually holds the line
72	
73	On this org's GitHub **`team`** plan, ruleset *metadata* rules (`tag_name_pattern`) are
74	Enterprise-only and silently **inert** — a malformed `v*` tag is not blocked at push time by a
75	ruleset. Naming is enforced by the hook and workflow below, not the rulesets. Three layers, in
76	order of reliability:
77	
78	1. **Pre-push hook** ([.husky/pre-push](../../.husky/pre-push) → [scripts/hooks/pre-push](../../scripts/hooks/pre-push))
79	   — *best-effort prevention*. Rejects a malformed `v*` tag before it leaves the developer's machine
80	   — the earliest catch, but bypassable (`git push --no-verify`, or a checkout without the hook
81	   installed), so not a hard guarantee. Allowed: `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`, `vX.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`.
82	   Non-`v*` tags and branch pushes pass through untouched.
83	2. **`tag-validate.yml`** ([.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml))
84	   — *detection*. Fails if a malformed `v*` tag lands on the remote (post-hoc alert, not a block).
85	3. **GitHub Rulesets** `tag-rc` (id 20487306) + `tag-release` (id 20487243) — enforce what core rules
86	   *can* on the `team` plan: **immutability** (`update` + `deletion` restricted) and **tier-1-only
87	   final tags** (`creation` restricted on `tag-release`, bypass = `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`).
88	   Their `tag_name_pattern` rules (`^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` and `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`)
89	   are **kept but inert on `team`** — they self-activate if the org ever upgrades to Enterprise.
90	
91	GitHub ruleset objects have no free-text description field, so the "inert on team" caveat can't
92	live on the ruleset itself — this section is its canonical record. The rulesets may optionally be
93	renamed in Settings → Rules to append " — naming inert on team plan" for an at-a-glance signal.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## Environment model — two categories
98	
99	| Category | Environments | How it deploys |
100	| --- | --- | --- |
101	| **Continuous / auto** | `dev`, `sit` | No human-picked tag. `dev` auto-deploys every `develop` merge; `sit` deploys the gate's commit via `workflow_run` off the SIT Gate on `release/**`. |
102	| **Tag-promoted / deliberate** | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | `workflow_dispatch` with a specific tag `ref`. Each can sit on a different tag simultaneously, decoupling their cadences. |
103	
104	**SIT stays branch/gate-driven** — its `workflow_run` trigger off the SIT Gate on `release/**` is
105	unchanged. This is an intentional exception to "every environment sits on a named tag": SIT is a
106	continuous auto-integration tier, the same category as `dev`, not a deliberate pinned-promotion
107	tier. Using tags is not the same as being triggered by a tag — tags and Releases still exist and are
108	visible; SIT simply auto-refreshes.
109	
110	**Environment names are the real GitHub Environment names** — `dev / test / sit / uat / staging /
111	prod`. Tooling must key off these, not the workflow-file suffix: `deploy-stg.yml` binds
112	`environment: staging` (the `stg`≠`staging` mismatch already caused a bug once).
113	
114	---
115	
116	## Downgrade protection (version-guard)
117	
118	[scripts/versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs), wired into the four tag-promoted
119	`deploy-*.yml` workflows:
120

122	  and **blocks** if `ref` is semver-older (`semver.lt`). Skips non-`v*` refs, allows the first-ever
123	  deploy, and **fails closed** on any lookup/parse error.
124	- **`record <env> <ref>`** runs *after* a successful push: stamps the deployed tag as an explicit
125	  GitHub Deployment (the auto-created Deployment records the *trigger* ref, not the deployed tag, so
126	  we record it ourselves and read it back).
127	- **`dev` and `sit` are excluded** — they have no human-picked `ref` to compare (consistent with the
128	  two-category model above).
129	- Guard/record key off the **GitHub Environment name** (`stg`→`staging`).

How releases are versioned, tagged, and promoted through the environments. This is the
day-to-day companion to the branch rules in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) (Branch Rules) and the
supervised-release flow in [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) —
this file covers **tags and promotion**, those cover **branches**.

---

## Tag taxonomy

Every deployable version is an **immutable, annotated git tag**. Environments deploy a specific
tag, never "whatever's on a branch right now."

| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Cut from | Who |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | Release candidate — a stabilising snapshot, cheap to iterate | `v0.1.0-rc.2` | a commit on `release/vX.Y.Z` | **any developer** |
| `vX.Y.Z` | Final release — the exact candidate that passed every gate | `v0.1.0` | the `release/vX.Y.Z` commit merged to `main` | **tier-1-approver only** |
| `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` | Emergency fix candidate, outside the normal train | `v0.1.1-hotfix.1` | a commit on `hotfix/vX.Y.Z` | **tier-1-approver only** |

**Versioning:**
- **MAJOR** locked at `0` pre-launch (SemVer reserves `0.y.z` for initial development). `v1.0.0`
  is reserved for **go-live**; MAJOR reverts to its normal rare-breaking-change meaning after.
- **MINOR** bumps once per sprint, when a new `release/vX.Y.Z` branch is cut — sprint 1 = `v0.1.0`,
  sprint 2 = `v0.2.0`.
- **PATCH** = bug-fix-only release against an already-shipped `MAJOR.MINOR` (e.g. a hotfix after
  `v0.1.0` → `v0.1.1`).
- The `-rc.N` counter is a plain incrementing number, **not** an environment reference — the same
  `v0.1.0-rc.1` can be on Test today and SIT tomorrow. Which environment saw which candidate is
  tracked via each `deploy-*.yml`'s Actions run history, not the tag name.
- The dot in `-rc.N` matters: SemVer compares `rc.10 > rc.2` numerically only as dot-separated
  fields; `rc10`/`rc2` would sort alphabetically (wrong). This is exactly what the version-guard
  relies on.

Non-`v*` tags are a separate namespace and unaffected by any of this: `sprint/{N}/{date}` (sprint
rollover, auto-cut by `deploy-dev.yml`) and any `sit/deploy/*` refs.

---

## Cutting a tag

Tags are cut with a **tag-only push** — a raw annotated `git tag`, then pushing the tag alone. We
deliberately avoid `npm version`: it creates a local `package.json`-bump *commit* alongside the tag,
and pushing that commit to the release branch is blocked by `release/**` branch protection
(`isAdminEnforced`, no bypass). Pushing only the tag sidesteps this — a tag push is not a branch
push. **Consequence:** `package.json`'s `version` field does not auto-track each candidate — it is
bumped once, deliberately, at the final-release PR.

**Release candidate (any developer):**

```bash
git checkout release/v0.1.0 && git pull
git tag -a v0.1.0-rc.0 -m "Release candidate v0.1.0-rc.0"
git push origin v0.1.0-rc.0           # tag only — NOT a branch push
gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0
```

- Always **annotated** (`-a -m`) — the tagger identity, timestamp, and message live in the tag
  object (`git show v0.1.0-rc.0`). Never lightweight.
- A tag push is not a branch push, so branch protection doesn't block it.

**Final release (tier-1-approver only):** cut `vX.Y.Z` on the release-branch commit being merged to
`main`, then promote it up UAT → Stage → Prod. Run [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)
at this point to produce the GitHub Release.

**Rollback is not a special case** — redeploy the previous known-good tag:
`gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f ref=v0.0.1`.

---

## Enforcement — what actually holds the line

On this org's GitHub **`team`** plan, ruleset *metadata* rules (`tag_name_pattern`) are
Enterprise-only and silently **inert** — a malformed `v*` tag is not blocked at push time by a
ruleset. Naming is enforced by the hook and workflow below, not the rulesets. Three layers, in
order of reliability:

1. **Pre-push hook** ([.husky/pre-push](../../.husky/pre-push) → [scripts/hooks/pre-push](../../scripts/hooks/pre-push))
   — *best-effort prevention*. Rejects a malformed `v*` tag before it leaves the developer's machine
   — the earliest catch, but bypassable (`git push --no-verify`, or a checkout without the hook
   installed), so not a hard guarantee. Allowed: `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`, `vX.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`.
   Non-`v*` tags and branch pushes pass through untouched.
2. **`tag-validate.yml`** ([.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml))
   — *detection*. Fails if a malformed `v*` tag lands on the remote (post-hoc alert, not a block).
3. **GitHub Rulesets** `tag-rc` (id 20487306) + `tag-release` (id 20487243) — enforce what core rules
   *can* on the `team` plan: **immutability** (`update` + `deletion` restricted) and **tier-1-only
   final tags** (`creation` restricted on `tag-release`, bypass = `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`).
   Their `tag_name_pattern` rules (`^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` and `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`)
   are **kept but inert on `team`** — they self-activate if the org ever upgrades to Enterprise.

GitHub ruleset objects have no free-text description field, so the "inert on team" caveat can't
live on the ruleset itself — this section is its canonical record. The rulesets may optionally be
renamed in Settings → Rules to append " — naming inert on team plan" for an at-a-glance signal.

---

## Environment model — two categories

| Category | Environments | How it deploys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Continuous / auto** | `dev`, `sit` | No human-picked tag. `dev` auto-deploys every `develop` merge; `sit` deploys the gate's commit via `workflow_run` off the SIT Gate on `release/**`. |
| **Tag-promoted / deliberate** | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | `workflow_dispatch` with a specific tag `ref`. Each can sit on a different tag simultaneously, decoupling their cadences. |

**SIT stays branch/gate-driven** — its `workflow_run` trigger off the SIT Gate on `release/**` is
unchanged. This is an intentional exception to "every environment sits on a named tag": SIT is a
continuous auto-integration tier, the same category as `dev`, not a deliberate pinned-promotion
tier. Using tags is not the same as being triggered by a tag — tags and Releases still exist and are
visible; SIT simply auto-refreshes.

**Environment names are the real GitHub Environment names** — `dev / test / sit / uat / staging /
prod`. Tooling must key off these, not the workflow-file suffix: `deploy-stg.yml` binds
`environment: staging` (the `stg`≠`staging` mismatch already caused a bug once).

---

## Downgrade protection (version-guard)

[scripts/versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs), wired into the four tag-promoted
`deploy-*.yml` workflows:

- **`check <env> <ref>`** runs *before* the push: reads the environment's last recorded deployed tag
  and **blocks** if `ref` is semver-older (`semver.lt`). Skips non-`v*` refs, allows the first-ever
  deploy, and **fails closed** on any lookup/parse error.
- **`record <env> <ref>`** runs *after* a successful push: stamps the deployed tag as an explicit
  GitHub Deployment (the auto-created Deployment records the *trigger* ref, not the deployed tag, so
  we record it ourselves and read it back).
- **`dev` and `sit` are excluded** — they have no human-picked `ref` to compare (consistent with the
  two-category model above).
- Guard/record key off the **GitHub Environment name** (`stg`→`staging`).

---

## The Test gate

`deploy-test.yml` runs **deploy-then-gate**: it deploys first (Test is the fast, disposable
quick-look tier), then a post-deploy gate verifies the same build. The run's overall pass/fail is the
**"safe to promote to SIT"** signal.

- **`bundle-size`** — `npm run test:max-file-size`, enforcing the `package.json` budgets
  (`main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB). Bundle-size is cheap, deterministic, and mobile
  page-speed is a top project priority, so bloat is caught at the earliest deployed tier.
- **P0 Playwright** — attaches to the same gate once a `*.p0.spec` exists (Lead QA, gherkin-first);
  it targets the Test storefront via the `test` env's `RETAIL_APP_HOME` variable.

This intentionally differs from SIT's **gate-then-deploy** (`digital-sit.yml`), which can hang a
pre-check on a `release/**` push event that Test doesn't have.

---

1	# Tagging & Environment Promotion
2	
3	How releases are versioned, tagged, and promoted through the environments. This is the
4	day-to-day companion to the branch rules in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) (Branch Rules) and the
5	supervised-release flow in [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) —
6	this file covers **tags and promotion**, those cover **branches**.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Tag taxonomy
11	
12	Every deployable version is an **immutable, annotated git tag**. Environments deploy a specific
13	tag, never "whatever's on a branch right now."
14	
15	| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Cut from | Who |
16	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
17	| `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | Release candidate — a stabilising snapshot, cheap to iterate | `v0.1.0-rc.2` | a commit on `release/vX.Y.Z` | **any developer** |
18	| `vX.Y.Z` | Final release — the exact candidate that passed every gate | `v0.1.0` | the `release/vX.Y.Z` commit merged to `main` | **tier-1-approver only** |
19	| `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` | Emergency fix candidate, outside the normal train | `v0.1.1-hotfix.1` | a commit on `hotfix/vX.Y.Z` | **tier-1-approver only** |
20	
21	**Versioning:**
22	- **MAJOR** locked at `0` pre-launch (SemVer reserves `0.y.z` for initial development). `v1.0.0`
23	  is reserved for **go-live**; MAJOR reverts to its normal rare-breaking-change meaning after.
24	- **MINOR** bumps once per sprint, when a new `release/vX.Y.Z` branch is cut — sprint 1 = `v0.1.0`,
25	  sprint 2 = `v0.2.0`.
26	- **PATCH** = bug-fix-only release against an already-shipped `MAJOR.MINOR` (e.g. a hotfix after
27	  `v0.1.0` → `v0.1.1`).
28	- The `-rc.N` counter is a plain incrementing number, **not** an environment reference — it counts
29	  candidate builds, not deployments. The same `v0.1.0-rc.1` can be deployed (and re-deployed) to
30	  Test on demand; which environment ran which candidate is tracked via each `deploy-*.yml`'s Actions
31	  run history, not the tag name.
32	- The dot in `-rc.N` matters: SemVer compares `rc.10 > rc.2` numerically only as dot-separated
33	  fields; `rc10`/`rc2` would sort alphabetically (wrong). This is exactly what the version-guard
34	  relies on.
35	
36	Non-`v*` tags are a separate namespace and unaffected by any of this: `sprint/{N}/{date}` (sprint
37	rollover, auto-cut by `deploy-dev.yml`) and any `sit/deploy/*` refs.
38	
39	---
40	
41	## Cutting a tag
42	
43	Tags are cut with a **tag-only push** — a raw annotated `git tag`, then pushing the tag alone. We
44	deliberately avoid `npm version`: it creates a local `package.json`-bump *commit* alongside the tag,
45	and pushing that commit to the release branch is blocked by `release/**` branch protection
46	(`isAdminEnforced`, no bypass). Pushing only the tag sidesteps this — a tag push is not a branch
47	push. **Consequence:** `package.json`'s `version` field does not auto-track each candidate — it is
48	bumped once, deliberately, at the final-release PR.
49	
50	**Release candidate (any developer):**
51	
52	```bash
53	git checkout release/v0.1.0 && git pull
54	git tag -a v0.1.0-rc.0 -m "Release candidate v0.1.0-rc.0"
55	git push origin v0.1.0-rc.0           # tag only — NOT a branch push
56	gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0
57	```
58	
59	- Always **annotated** (`-a -m`) — the tagger identity, timestamp, and message live in the tag
60	  object (`git show v0.1.0-rc.0`). Never lightweight.
61	- A tag push is not a branch push, so branch protection doesn't block it.
62	
63	**Final release (tier-1-approver only):** cut `vX.Y.Z` on the release-branch commit being merged to
64	`main`, then promote it up through `uat` → `staging` → `prod`. Run [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)
65	at this point to produce the GitHub Release.
66	
67	**Rollback is not a special case** — redeploy the previous known-good tag:
68	`gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f ref=v0.0.1`.
69	
70	---
71	
72	## Enforcement — what actually holds the line
73	
74	On this org's GitHub **`team`** plan, ruleset *metadata* rules (`tag_name_pattern`) are
75	Enterprise-only and silently **inert** — a malformed `v*` tag is not blocked at push time by a
76	ruleset. Naming is enforced by the hook and workflow below, not the rulesets. Three layers, in
77	order of reliability:
78	
79	1. **Pre-push hook** ([.husky/pre-push](../../.husky/pre-push) → [scripts/hooks/pre-push](../../scripts/hooks/pre-push))
80	   — *best-effort prevention*. Rejects a malformed `v*` tag before it leaves the developer's machine
81	   — the earliest catch, but bypassable (`git push --no-verify`, or a checkout without the hook
82	   installed), so not a hard guarantee. Allowed: `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`, `vX.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`.
83	   Non-`v*` tags and branch pushes pass through untouched.
84	2. **`tag-validate.yml`** ([.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml))
85	   — *detection*. Fails if a malformed `v*` tag lands on the remote (post-hoc alert, not a block).
86	3. **GitHub Rulesets** `tag-rc` (id 20487306) + `tag-release` (id 20487243) — enforce what core rules
87	   *can* on the `team` plan: **immutability** (`update` + `deletion` restricted) and **tier-1-only
88	   final tags** (`creation` restricted on `tag-release`, bypass = `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`).
89	   Their `tag_name_pattern` rules (`^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` and `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`)
90	   are **kept but inert on `team`** — they self-activate if the org ever upgrades to Enterprise.
91	
92	GitHub ruleset objects have no free-text description field, so the "inert on team" caveat can't
93	live on the ruleset itself — this section is its canonical record. The rulesets may optionally be
94	renamed in Settings → Rules to append " — naming inert on team plan" for an at-a-glance signal.
95	
96	---
97	
98	## Environment model — two categories
99	
100	| Category | Environments | How it deploys |
101	| --- | --- | --- |
102	| **Continuous / auto** | `dev`, `sit` | No human-picked tag. `dev` auto-deploys every `develop` merge; `sit` deploys the gate's commit via `workflow_run` off the SIT Gate on `release/**`. |
103	| **Tag-promoted / deliberate** | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | `workflow_dispatch` with a specific tag `ref`. Each can sit on a different tag simultaneously, decoupling their cadences. |
104	
105	**SIT stays branch/gate-driven** — its `workflow_run` trigger off the SIT Gate on `release/**` is
106	unchanged. This is an intentional exception to "every environment sits on a named tag": SIT is a
107	continuous auto-integration tier, the same category as `dev`, not a deliberate pinned-promotion
108	tier. Using tags is not the same as being triggered by a tag — tags and Releases still exist and are
109	visible; SIT simply auto-refreshes.
110	
111	**Environment names are the real GitHub Environment names** — `dev / test / sit / uat / staging /
112	prod`. Tooling must key off these, not the workflow-file suffix: `deploy-stg.yml` binds
113	`environment: staging` (the `stg`≠`staging` mismatch already caused a bug once).
114	
115	---
116	
117	## Downgrade protection (version-guard)
118	
119	[scripts/versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs), wired into the four tag-promoted
120	`deploy-*.yml` workflows:
121	
122	- **`check <env> <ref>`** runs *before* the push: reads the environment's last recorded deployed tag
123	  and **blocks** if `ref` is semver-older (`semver.lt`). Skips non-`v*` refs, allows the first-ever
124	  deploy, and **fails closed** on any lookup/parse error.
125	- **`record <env> <ref>`** runs *after* a successful push: stamps the deployed tag as an explicit
126	  GitHub Deployment (the auto-created Deployment records the *trigger* ref, not the deployed tag, so
127	  we record it ourselves and read it back).
128	- **`dev` and `sit` are excluded** — they have no human-picked `ref` to compare (consistent with the
129	  two-category model above).
130	- Guard/record key off the **GitHub Environment name** (`stg`→`staging`).
131	
132	---
133	
134	## The Test gate
135	
136	`deploy-test.yml` runs **deploy-then-gate**: it deploys first (Test is the fast, disposable

F4 first needs a real verdict, not a reflex skip. Let me V&V the claim.

**The finding:** the example does `git checkout release/v0.1.0 && git pull` then tags local `HEAD`. If local `release/v0.1.0` has diverged from origin, `git pull` creates a **merge commit**, `git tag` then tags *that local commit*, and the tag-only push publishes a tag pointing at a commit **never reviewed on origin** — so the deploy would run unreviewed code.

**Is it real?** Yes, technically:
- `git pull` = fetch + merge; on a diverged branch it produces a local merge commit (HEAD ≠ origin tip). Tagging HEAD then captures the un-pushed commit.
- It only bites if the local release checkout has diverged — which *shouldn't* happen on a protected release branch, but a stray local commit is enough to trigger it.

**Implement vs reply-only?** This is a **prescriptive governance doc** — the commands get copy-pasted verbatim. An example that can silently publish an unreviewed commit is a real footgun, and the fix is tiny and strictly safer. So my verdict: **implement** (not reply-only). Tag the fetched remote tip explicitly, which is immune to local state.

1	/**
2	 * versionGuard.mjs — downgrade protection for tag-based environment promotion.
3	 *
4	 * On the GitHub Team plan, a deploy's auto-created Deployment records the *trigger*
5	 * ref (the default branch), NOT the tag that was actually deployed. So we record the
6	 * deployed tag ourselves (an explicit GitHub Deployment) and read it back here to
7	 * block accidental downgrades on the manually-promoted tiers (test/uat/staging/prod).
8	 *
9	 * Usage (from a deploy-*.yml, after `npm install`, with GH_TOKEN set):
10	 *   node scripts/versionGuard.mjs check  <env> <ref>   # before push — block a downgrade
11	 *   node scripts/versionGuard.mjs record <env> <ref>   # after a successful push — record the tag
12	 *
13	 * <env> is the GitHub Environment name (test | uat | staging | prod).
14	 *
15	 * `check` behaviour:
16	 *   - <ref> is not a version tag       -> skip/allow (e.g. deploying a feature branch to Test)
17	 *   - <ref> not valid semver           -> fail closed (exit 1)
18	 *   - no prior tag on the env          -> allow (first deploy)
19	 *   - <ref> strictly older             -> BLOCK (exit 1)
20	 *   - <ref> equal or newer             -> allow
21	 *   - lookup error / invalid stored ref -> fail closed (exit 1)
22	 *
23	 * `record` skips non-version-tag refs; it FAILS the run if it cannot create the deployment record
24	 * (a missing baseline would let a later run downgrade), and only warns if the follow-up status
25	 * update fails (the ref is already recorded, which is what the guard reads).
26	 */
27	import {execFileSync} from 'node:child_process'
28	import semver from 'semver'

30	// vX.Y.Z with an optional -rc.N or -hotfix.N suffix (matches the repo tag rulesets).

38	    process.exit(1)
39	}

41	    console.log(`✓ version-guard: ${msg}`)

43	}

48	if (!repo) die('GITHUB_REPOSITORY is not set')
